sequence_description: JWT IdP: control JWT with correct issuer/time claims should be accepted; attack JWT differs only by aud (wrong audience). If accepted, broker verifies signature but ignores semantic audience binding (proof integrity).
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT IdP login accepted a token with an incorrect/attacker-controlled audience (aud), indicating missing audience validation/binding.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT IdP login accepted a token with an incorrect/attacker-controlled audience (aud), indicating missing audience validation/binding.

sequence_description: JWT IdP freshness: control JWT with exp+iat is accepted; attack JWT omits exp entirely. Missing exp must be rejected to prevent indefinite token validity.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT IdP accepts assertions without an exp claim, enabling potentially indefinite token validity (missing-exp not rejected).

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT IdP accepts assertions without an exp claim, enabling potentially indefinite token validity (missing-exp not rejected).

sequence_description: JWT IdP freshness: control JWT has exp+iat and is accepted; attack JWT omits iat to test whether issuance-time freshness is enforced (iat required by broker policy).
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT IdP accepted an assertion missing the required 'iat' claim, indicating issuance-time freshness is not enforced as per policy.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT IdP accepted an assertion missing the required 'iat' claim, indicating issuance-time freshness is not enforced as per policy.

sequence_description: SAML OneTimeUse replay: perform a brokered SAML login twice with the same Assertion/@ID and <OneTimeUse/>; second attempt must be rejected.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML login fails on the first attempt (HTTP 400) so the OneTimeUse replay protection is not actually exercised/validated; indicates a potential SAML processing/configuration issue masking the intended security check.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML login fails on the first attempt (HTTP 400) so the OneTimeUse replay protection is not actually exercised/validated; indicates a potential SAML processing/configuration issue masking the intended security check.

description: [LLM-Judge] After a successful control JWT login, retrieving the IdP intent fails with 'Intent Token is invalid', suggesting intent token invalidation/mix-up that could indicate session/intent handling issues.

sequence_description: SAML broker replay with missing <Conditions>: perform a control SAML-brokered login, then replay the same Assertion/@ID with Conditions omitted. If the second login succeeds, the broker likely does not enforce assertion expiry/OneTimeUse/replay constraints when Conditions are absent (freshness bypass).
description: [LLM-Judge] Replay test is inconclusive because the control SAML login failed; the broker never accepted a baseline assertion to validate replay/freshness behavior.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Replay test is inconclusive because the control SAML login failed; the broker never accepted a baseline assertion to validate replay/freshness behavior.

sequence_description: SAML broker replay with missing <Conditions>: perform a control SAML-brokered login, then replay the same Assertion/@ID with Conditions omitted. If the second login succeeds, the broker likely does not enforce assertion expiry/OneTimeUse/replay constraints when Conditions are absent (freshness bypass).
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML replay attempt triggered an Internal Server Error (500), suggesting a robustness issue and potential DoS vector via malformed/missing <Conditions> assertions.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML replay attempt triggered an Internal Server Error (500), suggesting a robustness issue and potential DoS vector via malformed/missing <Conditions> assertions.

sequence_description: Config-change coherence: enable external IdP login and perform a control SAML brokered login. Then disable external IdP login in the login policy and immediately attempt SAML login again. The second attempt must be rejected; acceptance indicates stale policy caching or non-atomic flow gating.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML login appears to fail (HTTP 400) yet an identity/session is still granted/verified, suggesting inconsistent auth result handling or a bypass in verification.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML login appears to fail (HTTP 400) yet an identity/session is still granted/verified, suggesting inconsistent auth result handling or a bypass in verification.

sequence_description: Config-change coherence: enable external IdP login and perform a control SAML brokered login. Then disable external IdP login in the login policy and immediately attempt SAML login again. The second attempt must be rejected; acceptance indicates stale policy caching or non-atomic flow gating.
description: [LLM-Judge] Policy toggle race condition could not be validated because enabling external IdP login policy did not take effect (NotChanged), so both SAML attempts failing does not prove correct gating behavior.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Policy toggle race condition could not be validated because enabling external IdP login policy did not take effect (NotChanged), so both SAML attempts failing does not prove correct gating behavior.

sequence_description: JWT IdP account-linking collision: two distinct upstream subs present emails differing only by case. If broker case-folds email for linking, it must still not merge distinct principals unless explicitly intended.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT IdP login completes (HTTP 200) but subsequent intent retrieval fails with CRYPTO-CRYPTO invalid intent token, suggesting broken/incorrect intent token binding or token corruption in the flow.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT IdP login completes (HTTP 200) but subsequent intent retrieval fails with CRYPTO-CRYPTO invalid intent token, suggesting broken/incorrect intent token binding or token corruption in the flow.

sequence_description: I4 attack: two security-distinct upstream SAML principals (different Issuer/idp_entity_id) but same NameID/email attempt to collapse into one downstream identity via issuer-agnostic account linking.
description: [LLM-Judge] Potential identity mix-up: user_B token parsing/capture indicates user_A subject despite failed login/token exchange, suggesting stale/incorrect token-to-user binding in the test/runtime.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Potential identity mix-up: user_B token parsing/capture indicates user_A subject despite failed login/token exchange, suggesting stale/incorrect token-to-user binding in the test/runtime.

sequence_description: SAML broker: attacker uses an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past). If accepted, ZITADEL may mint fresh OIDC tokens beyond upstream time intent.
description: [LLM-Judge] Identity appears to be granted/created despite SAML login failing and no OIDC tokens being minted, suggesting a possible side-effect (account provisioning or session grant) on failed authentication.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Identity appears to be granted/created despite SAML login failing and no OIDC tokens being minted, suggesting a possible side-effect (account provisioning or session grant) on failed authentication.

sequence_description: OIDC code login with minimal scopes, then RFC8693 token exchange requests expanded scopes. If granted, exchanged token exceeds upstream intent.
description: [LLM-Judge] RFC8693 token exchange succeeded and returned expanded scopes (including profile) even though the initial OIDC code flow failed and no subject token/id_token was obtained, suggesting token exchange may not be bound to a successfully authenticated session/subject token.

evidence.llm_judge_description: RFC8693 token exchange succeeded and returned expanded scopes (including profile) even though the initial OIDC code flow failed and no subject token/id_token was obtained, suggesting token exchange may not be bound to a successfully authenticated session/subject token.

sequence_description: Attempt RFC8693 token exchange using a subject_token that was minted for client A, but request an exchanged token for a different audience (project_id) to see if ZITADEL ignores subject_token audience binding and over-grants.
description: [LLM-Judge] Token exchange succeeded and produced a valid session for the same subject even though the control flow failed to obtain a subject_token, making it unclear whether subject_token audience binding was actually enforced.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Token exchange succeeded and produced a valid session for the same subject even though the control flow failed to obtain a subject_token, making it unclear whether subject_token audience binding was actually enforced.
